events.description: Jake Shimabukuro (born November 3, 1976, in Honolulu, Hawaii) is an American ukulele virtuoso and composer known for his fast and complex finger work. His music combines elements of jazz, blues, funk, rock, bluegrass, classical, folk, and flamenco. Shimabukuro has written numerous original compositions, including the entire soundtracks to two Japanese films, Hula Girls (2007) and the Japanese remake of Sideways (2009). Well known in Hawaii and Japan during his early solo career in the early 2000s, Shimabukuro became famous internationally in 2006, when a video of him playing a virtuosic rendition of "While My Guitar Gently Weeps" was posted on YouTube without his knowledge and became one of the first viral videos on that site. His concert engagements, collaborations with legendary musicians, media appearances, and music production have snowballed since then.

events.description:
Buy Tickets

Doors 6:30pm / Screening 7pm

$15 / free or discounted for members

Curated & presented by Bradford Nordeen in association with Dirty Looks, The Lab and San Francisco Cinematheque

This program was initially organized in collaboration between Dirty Looks and LA Filmforum

This screening is dedicated to Agosto Machado (????–2026)—“a lady never tells.”

Jack Smith was an underground visionary in every sense of the word. Jack poured glitter into everything he made: pasty creatures, plastic fantasias and moldy monsters. He was a performance artist, filmmaker, playwright, photographer, socialist, aesthete, installation artist, scene-stealer, writer, interventionist. He built a theater and movie-studio in his rickety loft out of street debris; an intricate and child-like universe, Cinemaroc, was equal parts Baroque and broke. For a contingency of art and theater fags and dolls, Jack, as Charles Ludlam once eloquently put it, “is the daddy of us all.” And quixotically, the fact that he remains a somewhat underground or cult figure, as opposed to canonized creature, attests to his legacy.

Best known as a filmmaker, Jack made wild, indeterminable pictures. Flaming Creatures was his first finished film. Well, in truth, it’s his only finished film, since it ricocheted out of his hands when a trend of underground film raids made his opus a trophy for either side of a decency debate. events.title: The Fretliners
events.description:
When The Kettle Sings Tour

The Fretliners

Thursday, December 10 | The Freight

There is something happening between the mountains and the plains. A stirring in the dust. A song rising from the timber. Out of that landscape of grit and grace comes The Fretliners, a band carrying forward the oldest tradition in American music: telling the truth.

You can call them Colorado’s next great acoustic act. You can point to their Telluride and RockyGrass New Artist wins. You can talk about their musicianship, their harmonies, or their ability to command a room. All of those things are true. But they only tell part of the story.

The Fretliners are carving their own path through American music, drawing from bluegrass, Americana, folk, and rock to create something that feels both familiar and completely their own. Their songs carry the weight of long roads, changing seasons, lost loves, and the quiet hope that keeps people moving forward.

What separates The Fretliners is not just how they play, but what they have to say. Their writing feels rooted in something older than trends. They sing about places that shaped them, people who stayed, memories that linger, and the moments that remind us we are still connected to something real.

There is a kind of honesty in their music that cannot be manufactured. Each note feels lived-in,like old wood worn smooth by generations of hands. Each lyric feels like a conversation around a fire, a story passed down because it still matters.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Storefront Church
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Storefront Church

Storefront Church is the project of Lukas Frank, who's drummed in Phoebe Bridgers' band and appeared on her albums, and the first song of his debut album As We Pass features DIIV frontman Cole Smith, but neither of those affiliations really prepares you for what to expect from As We Pass. It's a 9-song collection that's largely made up of bluesy, gothy, emo-y melancholic songs that sometimes sound like a cross between '90s Cure deep cuts and Nirvana Unplugged. (Lukas also cites Scott Walker as an influence, and you can hear that too.) Most of the album is bare-bones and somber, but Lukas also revs things up for the noise punk of "Faction from Under the Grove," and that fits right in too. With As We Pass, Lukas enters a long, line of depressive singer/songwriters, but even with over half a century of music like this, something about Lukas stands out. He grips you right off the bat with album opener "After the Alphabets" -- the kind of song that can make you drop everything and listen as soon as his voice comes in -- and the album stays that compelling throughout. Even with connections to established artists and the great Sargent House label behind him, this doesn't feel like the smash arrival of a hot new buzz artist; it's the subtle arrival of a songwriter whose songs creep up on you and knock you out when you're least expecting it. Usually, that's even better.

The New Yorker wrote that the record “reaches the pinnacle of a vibrant, harmonic enterprise.”

The arc of their catalog is one of continuous, confident evolution. Their debut, Wildewoman, announced a singular voice — dual lead vocals wrapped in retro charm, which The New York Times praised the live show that year as “the best musical performance of any kind.”

Good Grief introduced a sleeker, synth-driven palette, while Second Nature — produced by Brandi Carlile and Dave Cobb — was celebrated by the Los Angeles Times with its “lush synths and sleek disco grooves under the women’s laser-guided vocals.”

events.title: Inspiring Splendor
events.description: This December, the PWC joins forces with the Palo Alto Chamber Orchestra to perform Vivaldi’s beloved Gloria. Carrying forward this season of celebration of women, by women, we’ll perform pieces by several composers who continue to inspire us. In addition to Vivaldi’s masterwork, the second half of our winter program celebrates the season with sacred and contemporary holiday treasures. Experience the luminous anticipation of Elaine Hagenberg’s O Come Emmanuel, Joan Szymko’s spirited Hodie, and Ann Callaway’s radiant Alleluia, Vidimus Stellam, paired with the otherworldly textures of Cindy Cox’s Wakah-Chan. We uplift traditions of community, reflection, and peace through Bernice Johnson Reagon’s stirring Seven Principles and Karen Siegel’s contemplative Oseh Shalom. The festivities draw to a heartwarming close with the gentle tenderness of Eleanor Daley’s Lullaby Carol and the timeless splendor of John Rutter’s setting of Silent Night. Join us 30 minutes before each performance for a pre-concert talk, and stay for a post-concert reception.

events.title: Spike Sikes and His Awesome Hotcakes: Holiday show
events.description:
Just The Right Recipe… The most frequently heard comment after a Spike’s Awesome Hotcakes gig goes something like this –
“No one is making this kind of music anymore!”
But what, exactly, is “this kind of music?”
Like hotcakes themselves, it goes by many names. Soul. Swing. Rhythm & Blues. Jazz. Jump. It’s a sound that’s classic and simple, but when it’s done right, it hits the spot, and has you grinning from ear to ear. Spike has spent years searching for this sound.
From the Texas blues joints he cut his teeth in to the funky halls of New Orleans, he was always studying the music, trying to find just the right recipe. It makes perfect sense that he found his bandmates in Sonoma County, a music scene that has fostered many eclectic artists for decades.
What he didn’t know was how hungry audiences were for “this kind of music.” You might say they’ve been eating it up like…Hotcakes!

events.title: Understanding Attachment Trauma & Building Resilience with Mindfulness
events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
with Pawan Bareja, PhD and Diane Poole Heller
We begin life with a child’s open heart, full of trust, innocence, and pure joy. Yet, over time, the world leaves its marks. We often arrive at our meditation cushions carrying a lifetime of hidden grief, from the lingering ache of a breakup to the quiet sorrow of a loveless childhood. To protect ourselves from this attachment trauma, we build walls that close us off from the very people we wish to love.
This daylong is an invitation to return home to the pure love that is your true nature. We do not heal in isolation; we heal together. Our nervous systems are beautifully social, wired to find safety, warmth, and co-regulation in the presence of others.
If accepting love feels foreign, you can break those protective patterns. Through guided meditations, gentle reflection, and supportive group connections, we will mend broken bonds, navigate love and conflict, and rebuild our lasting resilience.
Diane will lead a practical teaching session drawing on her background in nervous-system-informed approaches to attachment, offering an embodied complement to the day’s content.

events.title: Eyes Wide Shut
events.description:
In IT’S A WONDERFUL LIFE, Jimmy Stewart’s George Bailey, at the height of his suicidal despair and panic, imagines a world in which he doesn’t exist. Stanley Kubrick goes one step further in sending Tom Cruise down an odyssey of sexual confusion and paranoia to learn the true meaning of Christmas.

Adapted from the Austrian short story Traumnovelle, Kubrick’s final film peeks us into the privileged world of Dr. Bill Hartford and his wife Alice (Cruise and Nicole Kidman), two well-to-do attractive socialites who, by all accounts, have it made. In a marijuana-fueled argument, Alice reveals thoughts of infidelity that send Bill into an existential panic, leading to an absurdist walkabout through New York that involves – you guessed it – a mysterious sex cult run by a shrouded aristocracy.

Did Kubrick make this to break up Cruise and Kidman’s marriage? How much did he know about mysterious sex trafficking rings? Did Sydney Pollack originate the shirtless-in-suspenders look? Clearly, the film poses more questions than it answers. For certain, EYES WIDE SHUT is a brutally funny sexscapade that puts an ellipses at the end of Kubrick’s storied career – and, most importantly – stands as a crucial text for our modern world. Fidelio!

events.description: This December, the PWC joins forces with the Palo Alto Chamber Orchestra to perform Vivaldi’s beloved Gloria. Carrying forward this season of celebration of women, by women, we’ll perform pieces by several composers who continue to inspire us. In addition to Vivaldi’s masterwork, the second half of our winter program celebrates the season with sacred and contemporary holiday treasures. Experience the luminous anticipation of Elaine Hagenberg’s O Come Emmanuel, Joan Szymko’s spirited Hodie, and Ann Callaway’s radiant Alleluia, Vidimus Stellam, paired with the otherworldly textures of Cindy Cox’s Wakah-Chan. We uplift traditions of community, reflection, and peace through Bernice Johnson Reagon’s stirring Seven Principles and Karen Siegel’s contemplative Oseh Shalom. The festivities draw to a heartwarming close with the gentle tenderness of Eleanor Daley’s Lullaby Carol and the timeless splendor of John Rutter’s setting of Silent Night. events.title: “Castro on Fire”: A Queer Resistance Walking Tour by Unspeakable Vice
events.description:
LOCATION

4127 18th Street

San Francisco, CA 94114

ADMISSION

RSVP and reserve tickets here

The GLBT Historical Society Museum is pleased to partner with Unspeakable Vice to offer a monthly walking tour focused on the history of LGBTQIA+ resistance in the Castro neighborhood. Created by tour guide, former senior adjunct professor, and practicing designer Shawn Sprockett, Unspeakable Vice began as a close look at the queer origins of San Francisco, traversing the city’s North Beach and Barbary Coast areas to trace the history through from 1770-1960. This new tour closes a three-part story, extending Sprockett’s detailed and engaging storytelling to the Castro neighborhood.

Ten years after the White Night riots, the police came back. Meet the trans man doctors turned away, the lesbians who ran the blood drives and wards, and the community that answered a plague and two police riots with the same refusal. This tour includes a free round at the Lookout, overlooking the neighborhood you've just walked.

Terrain: city sidewalks with one moderate hill; the Lookout is upstairs, stairs only

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: June McDoom
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

June McDoom

There is a hush most of us only knew as children, the warm drift between familiar household sounds and being carried to bed, a place that belongs to you and to some self you have not met yet. June McDoom's debut full-length, Follow the Light, lives in that dream space and then keeps walking, slipping out of time and waking somewhere new, barely familiar enough to feel like home yet wholly your own.

She came up in a Jamaican household on the edge of the Florida Everglades, an existence built of extended family, communal care, bass and harmonics. Her father, a carpenter and a student of sound, built his own speakers and kept three sound systems going across as many rooms. His low end would rise through her bedroom floor like some wayward cat while she lay above it with folk records, finding harmonies that were new and hers alone. Two musics in one room. Lushness as past and premonition.

She found folk on her own, somewhere between the cast recording of The Sound of Music and Simon and Garfunkel, while everyone around her called it sleepy music. She did not mind being the only one. The solitude let her fall for harmony first, before words, before anything else, and harmony is still the thing she reaches for.

Generationally speaking, the music was already in the air. Her grandfather, Colin Smith, is a distinguished mento man who played banjo and guitar and built his own rumba boxes, worked to keep Jamaica's oldest acoustic folk form alive....

events.title: Little Women (2019)
events.description:
Having already once revolutionized the coming-of-age story with her debut LADY BIRD, Greta Gerwig has somehow outdone herself with this gorgeous and thoroughly original rendition of the beloved Louisa May Alcott classic. Bringing her effusive humor, authenticity, and irresistible warmth to the otherwise mannered Civil War-era New England, Gerwig's adaptation of LITTLE WOMEN breathes visceral new life into the March sisters – portraying them as unique, complicated, flawed, and astonishingly human. So human that you will leave the theater wanting to text Jo March and, for several reasons, this will not be a possibility.

You may also find it physically impossible not to chef's kiss at the cast, which is as close to pitch-perfect as it gets. Starring Saoirse Ronan as Jo, Emma Watson as Meg, Florence Pugh as Amy, and Eliza Scanlen as Beth, LITTLE WOMEN also features Laura Dern (!), Meryl Streep (!), Bob Odenkirk (!), and Timothée Chalamet as the dashing but lovelorn Laurie (!!!).

Save for a fireworks show, sky-written ode, or Mount Rushmore-type situation, we cannot recommend this rich, heartrending wonder of a film anymore. Its timeless charm is sure to capture the hearts of little women (and men) everywhere.

If you ever feel as if music has lost its capacity for surprise, the beguiling wonder and infinite creativity of Yaelokre will respark your belief. The Filipino-Icelandic artist – real name Keath Ósk (they/it) – fuses three imaginative strands to their visionary expression: intimate, innocent folk infused with leftfield surrealism and instant pop accessibility; artwork which is intricately detailed and beautifully alluring; and storytelling which brings personal experience and poetry into rich, fable-like narratives. What’s more, all three of these elements are crafted by this one visionary artist.

The scale of the fantastical world they have created is vast, both in terms of narrative and lore. But its essence is relatively simple. The songs are set in the fictional world of Meadowlark and chart the adventures of four masked children who comprise a musical ensemble known at The Lark: Cole Seymour, Clémente Dearworth, Peregrine August, and Kingsley. They perform as representatives of The Harkers, mythical beings who express the fundamental principles of nature, wonder and chaos. What’s more, Yaelokre voices all of the different characters within their universe.

events.title: Bitter Christmas
events.description:
Check out IN THE MOOD FOR ALMODÓVAR, our limited series celebrating three earlier works by Pedro Almodóvar.

The incomparable Almodóvar has been rendering the life of the creative mind on screen for five decades, with exquisite attention to every nuance of both aesthetic design and human emotion. With his complexly conceived latest, he uses a metacinematic framework to explore the artist’s tenuous relationship between fiction and reality. The sublimely expressive Bárbara Lennie stars as Elsa, a well-known actress suffering from debilitating migraines whose directorial efforts had failed upon release but have become cult classics. While trying to maintain a relationship with her loyal boyfriend Bonifacio (Patrick Criado), a fireman moonlighting as a stripper, she becomes inspired by the travails of her friends to write a new script.

Yet Elsa’s story is itself a story—being written by Raúl (Leonardo Sbaraglia), an Almodóvar-esque filmmaker who is, in turn, taking his cues from the lives of those around him. Mixing the irreverence of early Almodóvar with the somber melodrama of his later work, Bitter Christmas insightfully details the vampiric nature of artistic creation and how we use fiction to try and right the wrongs of our lives.

“With its moving musical interludes, comic patter and outrageously chic production design, Bitter Christmas is another dazzling, late-period jewel” — Little White Lies

For two decades, Pokey LaFarge has walked his own effortlessly cool road as an exceptionally iconoclastic troubadour – forthright, genuine, and markedly keen to put it all out there. Rent Money now sees him pushing forward yet again in what can be safely declared his finest collection to date, both as an heartfelt expression of personal experience and as no-nonsense social commentary. With its twanging guitars, plucky rhythms, and undeniably captivating melodies, the album soars and swings, its joyous refrains belying the inescapable undercurrent of constant worry and angst that permeates these troubled times. As always, the Illinois native deftly traverses the genre boundaries, seamlessly integrating the myriad strains of 20th-century American music with a freewheeling command of earnest songcraft, inspired performance, and subversive creativity. Rent Money stands tall as an indisputable high-water mark for Pokey LaFarge – a defining collection from a one-of-a-kind artist of rare ingenuity and uncommon candor, now as ever, determinedly crafting a sure-footed brand of deeply human music all his own.

“People are always going to tell you what they think you should play,” says Pokey LaFarge, “what you should sing about, how you should sound, how you should look, how you should act. And I’ve always just been like, nah. Nope. I’ve just completely gone my own way, and...

events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Robber Robber

Pinpointing the specific catalyst for an avalanche can be slippery — any combination of classic elements, human interference, or freak accident can trigger disaster — and documenting these precise moments often rests on serendipitous reflexes. On Two Wheels Move the Soul, Robber Robber offer themselves as ignition and capture every sound in the wake. Involuntarily thrust into the throws of rootless nomadism, Robber Robber ringleader Nina Cates collects a series of pressurized vignettes to assemble the Burlington quartet’s thrillingly explosive sophomore album.

Two Wheels Move the Soul was written and recorded throughout the winter of 2024 and 2025, a season of Cates’ life characterized by near-constant upheaval. In January of 2025, Cates (and Robber Robber co-founder) Zack James were displaced from their longtime home at the behest of a landlord’s call to have their building demolished. In a moment’s notice — and amidst a particularly brutal Vermont winter — Cates and James were left to fend for themselves. Luckily, the two were able to tap a deep well of support within their community, finding respite on the couches of Lily Seabird, Greg Freeman, and Thus Love’s Echo Mars. An unused attic provided their longest arrangement.

The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu.

Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. events.description:
Marin Shakespeare Company presents The Secret Garden, adapted by Jon Tracy from Frances Hodgson Burnett’s beloved novel and directed by Jennifer Le Blanc.
After losing her parents, 10-year-old Mary Lennox arrives at her uncle’s Yorkshire estate. A hidden garden draws her into new friendships—and into the difficult work of learning how to care for someone beyond herself. Behind the estate’s locked doors, her cousin Colin and his father must find their own ways toward connection and belonging.
Five performers create the world of the house, the moor, and the garden through movement, song, and sound. This faithful yet freshly illuminated adaptation honors the wonder of Burnett’s story while making room for each person to grow on their own terms.
A family production especially suited to school-age children, teens, and adults, The Secret Garden offers warmth and wonder alongside themes of parental loss, grief, isolation, and disability.

events.title: Whitney Johnson, Lia Kohl, Macie Stewart + Marguerite Brown
events.description:
Buy Tickets

Doors 8pm / Show 8:30pm

$23 / free or discounted for members

Whitney Johnson, Lia Kohl, and Macie Stewart are a trio who utilize string instruments, voices, and manual tape effect processing to craft compositions from alternately tranquil and disquieting improvised music. The three musicians are individually rooted in deep sound exploration, multi-disciplinary composition, and all manner of cross-genre collaboration. The musical ground covered by their solo practices is correspondingly expansive, and their individual recording and performance credits read as a veritable who’s who, ranging from DIY darlings to household names of experimental avant-garde, electronic, indie rock, and more.

Their influences are vast — dispatched with more playful ease than a trio of string instruments is typically approached with, and just as likely to be found in the cloud-obscured mountains of Donegal, the low-rent cacophony of a Midwestern basement, or the revelatory expanse of the Nurse With Wound list as in the storied halls of the academy. Touchstones and areas of interest aside, the main thing that Johnson, Kohl, and Stewart engage with in BODY SOUND is: listening and reacting.

Marguerite Brown is a composer/performer who explores new mediums, forms, and performance practices with an emphasis on unorthodox approaches to tuning and temperament. tuning to is an ever-evolving solo set that explores the electric guitar as a celestial body using a curated set of planetary tunin...

events.venue: Marin Art and Garden Center in Ross
events.address: 30 Sir Francis Drake Blvd, Ross, CA, 94957
events.description:
Friday, December 18 * 12 PM - 2 PM

Use foraged materials and festive extras to create your own holiday cards, for loved ones or just for fun!

Join Marin-based photographer and printmaker Ben Davidson and photo teacher and artist Laurie Reemsnyder for a creative printmaking workshop using botanical material gathered from the garden grounds and Marin's hills and forests to make playful, seasonal cards for the holidays.

We start with a 20-minute "foraging" walk around the 11-acre garden, collecting evergreen sprigs, seed pods, dried leaves, and other winter treasures. Then we head to the Cottage for a 60-minute printmaking session, using the cyanotype (photo) process if the day is sunny. On an overcast day, we will use our plant material to create elegant botanical stencil prints.

All participants will make cards to bring home, and will also receive a wooden frame to showcase their favorite creation from this fun and informative nature walk and printmaking workshop.

$55.09.

events.title: Venna
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
Venna

Friday, December 8 | The Castro

After two EPs and an illuminating start to his career, Grammy Award-winning saxophonist Venna releases his debut album, MALIK.

For Venna, it’s been a whirlwind of a journey to arrive at this point. He’s spent the better part of three years on the road touring, while coming back to London intermittently. In the spaces he finds himself in as a musician, he’s often the youngest in the room. This period gave him the confidence to embark on this next stage of his career.

“Every experience, every memory, every conversation, anything new, any encounter has influenced how this album sounds. I might like a particular guitar tone from it, and then I bring it into my world. Everything has come and conjured into one place, and it’s beautiful to also hear and see,” Venna says.

Speaking on how he found the words to sing: “Does anyone really have the words to say? I don’t know. I don’t know if I had the words to say. I just conjured words and thoughts and tried to make art out of it.”

Featuring vocals from Jorja Smith, Cari, Leon Thomas, Smino, MIKE, and himself, MALIK is where listeners can get lost and find themselves again. The album also features a long list of musicians including Rocco Palladino, Elijah Fox, AoD, J Warner, Marco Bernardis and longtime collaborator, Yussef Dayes.

MALIK embodies the melting pot of sounds that reflects Venna’s environment. Venna doesn’t want to be rooted in jazz alone; his...

events.title: Florencia Ramirez, The Kitchen Activist
events.description:
Saturday, December 19, 2026, 11:00 am - 11:45 am

Stop by the Foodwise Classroom for a cooking demo featuring the seasonal bounty of the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market.

Florencia Ramirez is the author of The Kitchen Activist: Your Step-by-Step Guide to Creating a Planet Smart Kitchen and Eat Less Water: The Solution to Water Shortages is in the Kitchen. A storyteller at heart and researcher by training, she holds a masters degree in public policy from the University of Chicago. Through writing, research, and lived experience, she explores how the everyday choices we make in our kitchens can become acts of environmental and social change. Her work has been featured on NPR, PBS, KTLA, CBS, KCRWs Good Food, and in the Los Angeles Times. She is the founder and Executive Director of the Pesticide Free Soil Project and the recipient of the Environmental Hero Award and the Gift of Freedom Award in Creative Nonfiction. Married and the mother of three Kitchen Activists, she splits her time between Oxnard, California, and Santa Fe, New Mexico.

All demos take place in the Foodwise Classroom (green tent in front of the Ferry Building) and are free to the public, with recipes and samples for all.

The demo will be followed by a book signing with book sales courtesy of Book Passage

The San Jose Nutcracker takes place in San Jose at the turn of the last century. events.title: Skip the Small Talk Night at Fluid510
events.description:
We've all heard that making friends is hard, loneliness is an epidemic, and the internet is making us forget how to be humans. So let's actually do something about it and talk to other human beings!
You'll pair up with the other nice people who showed up and switch partners every so often (kinda like speed-dating, but without the speed and without the dating). Our host will lead the whole shebang, and we'll give you question cards to take the conversation a few notches deeper so you don't accidentally talk about what you do for work six times in a row.
Come solo or bring a friend. You can always skip a question and choose how much you share. This is a friendship event.

events.title: Robert Glasper
events.description:
Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing.

Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu.

Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz...

events.title: Elvin Bishop
events.address: 417 Alvarado Street, Monterey, CA, Monterey, CA, 93940
events.description:
Ever since Rock & Roll and Blues Hall Of Famer Elvin Bishop first hit the scene with the Paul Butterfield Blues Band back in 1965, he's blazed his own musical trail. Whether he was playing raw, eye-popping blues, or penning the evergreen radio hit Fooled Around And Fell In Love, or touring the world for decades delivering his original, good-time countrified blues, Bishop has always inspired his fans with his rowdy guitar playing and witty, slice-of-life songs. Rolling Stone calls Bishop "a legendary guitarist" whose playing is "impeccable and spirited...a distinguished American player."

Late in 2015, Elvin Bishop formed The Big Fun Trio, with Bishop on guitar and vocals, and his friends Bob Welsh on piano and guitar and Willy Jordan on cajón (a hand-played Peruvian drumbox) and vocals. After playing just a handful of live dates, the group's instantly crowd-pleasing music and undeniable chemistry took the blues world by storm. With the release of their self-titled CD in 2017, media and fan response was immediate and overwhelming. DownBeat celebrated Bishop's "verbal hijinks, outstanding guitar work and country boy friendliness." OffBeat said The Big Fun Trio was "intricate, funky and uplifting," declaring them, "consistently great." With its top-shelf musicianship and front-porch vibe, the album earned a Grammy Award nomination.

The Big Fun Trio quickly discovered the more they played live, the more fun they had making music together. So a follow-up recording was an easy dec...

events.description:
Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing.

Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu.

Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz...

Set during Christmastime in 1950s New York, Todd Haynes’ adaptation of Patricia Highsmith’s The Price of Salt centers on shy, aspiring photographer Therese Belivet (Rooney Mara), whose world changes when she meets the elegant Carol Aird (Cate Blanchett). As Carol struggles to maintain custody of her daughter amid a heated divorce, she and Therese develop a secret-yet-passionate romance that changes them both irrevocably.

Featuring a stunning screenplay from Phyllis Nagy; memorable supporting turns from Sarah Paulson, Kyle Chandler, and Jake Lacy; and wholly transportive production design and costuming, Carol remains one of queer cinema’s most exquisite films.

events.title: Red Rocket
events.description:
Burnt out by the LA adult film scene, washed-up porn star Mikey Saber (Simon Rex) heads back to his old stomping grounds in small-town Texas. After a not-so-successful attempt at reconnecting with his estranged wife, Lexi (Bree Elrod), he forms an instant connection with Strawberry (Suzanna Son). Soon he’s juggling jealous exes, new love, and drug-dealing locals, all with a smile on his face. Who says you can’t go home again?

The audacious new film from writer-director Sean Baker (THE FLORIDA PROJECT, TANGERINE), starring Simon Rex in a magnetic, live-wire performance, RED ROCKET is a darkly funny and humane portrait of a uniquely American hustler and the hometown that barely tolerates him.

events.title: El Grupo de Apoyo Latino
events.description:
El Grupo de Apoyo Latino de SFAF es un grupo social y educativo que ofrece un espacio abierto, seguro, y confidencial para apoyar a la comunidad Latina afectada por el VIH y SIDA. Es un grupo diverso, donde el respeto es la base para que todos los asistentes puedan expresar libremente sus experiencias, identidad, étnicidad, nacionalidad, sexualidad, y creencias religiosas.

events.title: P L A Y E R S L A Y O V E R
QUEERSADA 2026: A Queer Posada
events.description:
A catered meal, chosen family vibes, and a place to kick it, all on Christmas Day.

For the fourth year, our annual FREE community meal returns!
It's a party, with catered food, movies on the screens, and chosen family vibes all afternoon.

We'll have pozole, pan con pavo, and more on the menu. The bar will be open (cash and credit card accepted) for any drinks you need. The food is on us, the drinks are on you.

How can you contribute? Bring a dessert you think people would like. Anything is a good thing!

And here's the thing: whether you celebrate the holiday or not isn't what we are concerned with.

The reality is, this can be a very challenging day for our community. Isolation, disconnection, hunger...

There is no reason we can't come together to make sure everybody has a safe, affirming place to go, and a good, dignified meal to eat, all in a familiar space.

And that's the thing: community is for everyone, regardless of age, income, professional or academic background, body type, and so on.

Questions? Follow us on IG and send us a DM: @boss.ideahouse

The event is free, but we are asking for each person coming to RSVP so we can keep an eye on the food and seating availability.

events.title: Vienna Teng
events.description:
Vienna Teng

Sunday, December 27 | The Freight

Some songs are the life of the party. Vienna Teng's are the back-porch conversation you still remember years later.

Her subversive choral piece "The Hymn of Acxiom” turns up in media literacy classes as well as drum corps shows (plus David Byrne’s blog, and the occasional flash mob choir in government buildings). The angst and effervescence in “Stray Italian Greyhound” has inspired anime music videos - and bridge-building political conversations.

Americana-tinged "City Hall" has quietly become a queer anthem, a soundtrack for coming-out journeys. The electro-pop exhortations of “Level Up” have powered many a doctoral dissertation, first novel, and courageous battle with illness. “Harbor” is a beloved first dance at weddings and a graduation gift. “Lullabye For A Stormy Night” has been woven into countless bedtime rituals. These are songs that not only age well, but remain trusted friends throughout people’s lives.

It helps that Vienna's sound has never stood still. Her warm, delicate mezzo has drawn listeners since 2002, when her debut Waking Hour landed appearances on NPR's Weekend Edition, The Late Show with David Letterman, and the top of Amazon’s charts. But she’s built different worlds around that voice from album to album: the string-laced intimacy of Warm Strangers, the hushed jazz of Dreaming Through the Noise, the eclectically ambitious Inland Territory, the shimmering electronica of Aims.

She’s world-built for othe...

events.title: The Apartment
events.description:
A young upstart, C.C. Baxter (Jack Lemmon), will do anything to move up in the world...even loan out his apartment to the higher-ups for their romantic flings and extramarital trysts. All seems relatively fine and dandy until C.C. finds a romance of his own.

Billy Wilder is a genius – there aren't enough words in the world to describe all the films he's made and express how much he means to cinema – but in 1960, Wilder wrote and directed a perfect movie. I'm not saying this to sell you on the idea of seeing this film at the Alamo; I'm stating it as a fact. There are very few instances where you watch a movie and realize you are witnessing pure magnificence in that moment. Sometimes you think about a movie after the fact, and it gets better and better until you begin to love a movie you previously only really liked. THE APARTMENT is NOT one of those movies. It is a movie where, within 15 minutes of watching, you realize it is unlike anything you have ever seen before. Jack Lemmon is amazing, Shirley MacLaine is a full-on pixie dream girl, and the chemistry and dialogue snap and sparkle like you wouldn't believe.

An alcoholic, out-of-work teacher takes a job as the wintertime caretaker of a snowy resort. He brings his wife and young son with him. He wants to get some writing done. Things take a very dark turn...

THE SHINING transcends any trappings of paperback adaptation or genre exercise to become one of the most elementally terrifying works of art of the 20th century. Come lose yourself in its marvelous madness on the big screen, where it forever belongs.

That’s not the case for Harry and Sally. In fact, when they meet, they don’t particularly like each other. Sally is earnest and good. Harry is cynical and depressive. It’s not a match made in heaven.

With an absurdly star-studded cast, including Pierce Brosnan, Glenn Close, Annette Bening, Danny DeVito, Michael J. Fox, Martin Short, Natalie Portman, Jack Black, Sarah Jessica Parker's head on a chihuahua’s body, and Jack Nicholson in two different roles, MARS ATTACKS! is a demented piece of retro-pop madness that represents Tim Burton at his very best. If you've never seen this epic, raucously funny cult classic, don't miss your chance to experience it on the big screen.

Following their electrifying run on the Sessanta tour alongside A Perfect Circle and Puscifer, Primus will return this summer with the Onward & Upward Tour—an expansive, coast-to-coast trek that marks an exciting new chapter for the band. events.title: Megalopolis
events.description:
Like the famed empire that Francis Ford Coppola’s epic passion project is styled after, MEGALOPOLIS is a towering, monumental spectacle that most people will think about at least once a day. The City of New Rome is at a crossroads. At one end sits Cesar Catilina (Adam Driver), the idealistic artist striving for a utopian future, and at the other sits Mayor Franklin Cicero (Giancarlo Esposito), a powerful figure perpetuating greed, special interests, and partisan warfare. Their titanic struggle will shake the foundations of their city and lay the groundwork for a new tomorrow.

As engrossing and ambitious as you would expect from the filmmaker behind THE GODFATHER and APOCALYPSE NOW, MEGALOPOLIS is an unforgettable vision that could only have come from Coppola. Of course, he didn’t do it alone, and everyone in the unbelievable cast (including Driver, Esposito, Nathalie Emmanuel, Aubrey Plaza, Laurence Fishburne, and more) delivers some of the most memorable performances of their careers.

events.title: Lord Huron
events.description:
Lord Huron was created by Los Angeles-based artist Ben Schneider in 2010. After writing and recording two independent EPs (Into the Sun and Mighty) on his own, demand grew for Lord Huron to perform live. Schneider recruited friends Mark Barry (percussion), Miguel Briseño (bass) and Tom Renaud (guitar). Having first played music together at the tender age of 12, the group reunited and quickly hit their stride, transforming the project into a full-fledged live band.

Lord Huron’s debut LP Lonesome Dreams was released in 2012 followed by Strange Trails in 2015. The latter featured the multi-platinum single “The Night We Met,” which has gone on to become one of Spotify’s Top 40 most-streamed songs of all time. In 2018, Lord Huron earned widespread critical acclaim and a Top 5 debut on the Billboard Top 200 with their third album, Vide Noir– while their following LP Long Lost garnered praise from NPR, Time, Los Angeles Times, Spin and Stereogum and sparked performances on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Jimmy Kimmel Live!, The Late Late Show with James Corden and CBS This Morning: Saturday. Their latest album The Cosmic Selector Vol. 1 was released in 2025 and brought the band’s live show into their largest venues to date, including Madison Square Garden in NYC and the Kia Forum in Los Angeles.

events.title: Lord Huron
events.description:
Lord Huron was created by Los Angeles-based artist Ben Schneider in 2010. After writing and recording two independent EPs (Into the Sun and Mighty) on his own, demand grew for Lord Huron to perform live. Schneider recruited friends Mark Barry (percussion), Miguel Briseño (bass) and Tom Renaud (guitar). Having first played music together at the tender age of 12, the group reunited and quickly hit their stride, transforming the project into a full-fledged live band.

Lord Huron’s debut LP Lonesome Dreams was released in 2012 followed by Strange Trails in 2015. The latter featured the multi-platinum single “The Night We Met,” which has gone on to become one of Spotify’s Top 40 most-streamed songs of all time. In 2018, Lord Huron earned widespread critical acclaim and a Top 5 debut on the Billboard Top 200 with their third album, Vide Noir– while their following LP Long Lost garnered praise from NPR, Time, Los Angeles Times, Spin and Stereogum and sparked performances on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Jimmy Kimmel Live!, The Late Late Show with James Corden and CBS This Morning: Saturday. Their latest album The Cosmic Selector Vol. 1 was released in 2025 and brought the band’s live show into their largest venues to date, including Madison Square Garden in NYC and the Kia Forum in Los Angeles.

Live On The Stoop began as a series of pop-up shows in the Fillmore District with The Top Chefs, a collective of musicians rooted in the city. events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
2001: A Space Odyssey (in 70mm)

Friday, January 8 | The Castro

Kick off the new year with the ultimate cinematic journey. On Friday, January 8, 2027, Stanley Kubrick’s masterwork 2001: A Space Odyssey returns to the historic The Castro Theatre for an exclusive, large-format screening presented in glorious 70mm.

An imposing black structure provides a connection between the past and the future in this enigmatic adaptation of a short story by revered sci-fi author Arthur C. Clarke. When Dr. Dave Bowman (Keir Dullea) and other astronauts are sent on a mysterious mission, their ship’s computer system, HAL, begins to display increasingly strange behavior, leading up to a tense showdown between man and machine that results in a mind-bending trek through space and time.

With its themes of humanity vs. machinery, 2001: A Space Odyssey serves as a timelier-than-ever cautionary tale about the human race’s never-ending thirst for technological advancement. Don’t miss your chance to see this sci-fi classic on the Castro screen!

Submitted by the Event OrganizerProfs and Pints Alameda presents: “Unhealthy Diets by Design,” on how cigarette science made us crave food that’s bad for us, with Laura Schmidt, professor of health policy and emeritus professor of psychiatry at the University of California San Francisco and scholar of the relationship between marketing and chronic disease.
It’s no accident that kids everywhere gobble down Lunchables, many of us can’t eat just one Oreo, and warnings by health experts and our own physicians often fail to deter us from loading our shopping carts with ultra-processed foods or pulling up to fast-food restaurants.

The truth is that our cravings for unhealthy foods are the product of extensive research, as well as deliberate manufacturing and marketing decisions, informed by lessons learned by Big Tobacco.
Get the inside skinny on how we’ve been manipulated into eating what makes many of us fat with Laura Schmidt, a highly respected sociologist and public health expert dedicated to understanding how modern lifestyles and economic pressures have driven the rise of chronic disease around the world.
Dr. Schmidt was one of several authors of a recent series of articles in the American Journal of Public Health examining how ultra-processed foods became a huge part of American diets. events.title: Las Migas
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerWith over 20 years of career and six studio albums, Las Migas have become one of the most internationally acclaimed Spanish bands. They have performed in more than 50 countries, including the United States, India, France, Egypt, Mexico, Cuba, Italy, Namibia, Jamaica, Algeria, Hong Kong, Germany, Chile, Sweden, Ukraine, and Morocco, among many others.
They have been nominated four times for the Latin Grammy Award in the Best Flamenco Album category (2016, 2022, 2024, and 2025), winning the award twice. They have also received the prestigious MIN Award in 2019 and 2023 for their albums Rumberas and Libres, respectively.

In the spring of 2025, Las Migas released Flamencas, a tribute to the essence and purity of flamenco. In this work, the band evolves its sound toward a more contemporary expression, wrapped in a powerful visual identity already showcased in the video for “Celos,” directed by renowned fashion photographer Javier Biosca. The recording won the Latin Grammy Award for Best Flamenco Album.

Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

events.description:

Join us on Wednesday, November 18th at the Eureka Valley Rec Center, where housing activist Robert Fruchtman will explain the “circuit breaker” built into the Family Zoning Plan to ensure the city hits its housing goals.

events.title: Free Astronomy Talk: Chile’s Giant Observatories (Randall Museum)
events.description:
The San Francisco Amateur Astronomers invite you to this free public event.
Chile is home to many of the largest and most advanced observatories on Earth, due to high altitudes, dry deserts, and low light pollution. Chile has become a center of cutting edge astronomical research, but this has been made possible by the collaborative efforts of multiple countries and the work of scientists and engineers from around the globe. This past summer I had the opportunity to participate in the Astronomy in Chile Educator Ambassadors Program (ACEAP). The program took me to the major observatories (ALMA, Vera Rubin, Gemini South, and more) and met many of the people who keep the observatories running. I’ll be sharing my insights into Chile, international astronomical collaborations, and the southern skies.
Brian “Astro” Castro is an amateur astronomer in San Francisco known for his pop-up sidewalk astronomy events in The Mission, around SF, and occasionally around the world. From 4” travel scopes that fit in a carry-on with room to spare, to 16” Dobsonians, he has shown the cosmos to over 15,000 people. He has organized for the local chapter of The Planetary Society, solo traveled to Guatemala to personally donate telescopes to schools and instruct in their use, and even strapped a large telescope to a bicycle trailer and biked around showing Saturn to festival goers at Burning Man in the Black Rock Desert. He is a 2025 ACEAP Ambassador

events.title: Accelerating Research and Engineering with AI
events.venue: Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing, UC Berkeley
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSimons InstituteLarge language models are now increasingly used to accelerate many research and engineering activities, thanks to their broad world knowledge and ability to work with arbitrary data. They have had great success in programming and math, and are being applied to biology, chemistry, and many other areas. But what are the strengths and limitations of AI for these tasks, and how can we make it even better? Matei Zaharia will describe research from UC Berkeley and other groups on using AI for engineering and research, including algorithms that use AI to search for better solutions to a problem (e.g., GEPA, AlphaEvolve, and AdaEvolve), and results researchers have been getting with them in computer science, biology, and other areas. In general, AI can be trained and applied effectively when solutions are easy to verify, but it has a much harder time when they aren’t (e.g., in chemistry and biology, where experiments take days). We are also getting better, however, at translating more problems into the easy-to-verify setting. In this Theoretically Speaking public lecture, Zaharia will discuss where this might lead, based on the trends we are seeing so far, and how science and engineering might look in the future when we have highly effective, tireless AI coworkers to explore solutions for us.
Matei Zaharia is an Associate Professor of EECS at UC Berkeley and Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer of Databricks. He is best known as the...

Europe on Screen. In Dialogue. In Celebration.
Discover the best of European feel-good cinema in San Francisco! From 19–23 November, the second edition of Ode to Joy: European CineFest San Francisco brings the stories, cultures and creativity of 17 European countries to the big screen at the Delancey Street Foundation.

Following last year’s successful inaugural festival, which welcomed more than 1,000 attendees, this year’s edition offers an expanded programme of uplifting, entertaining and engaging European films. From comedy and family-friendly stories to music, drama and inspiring real-life journeys, there is something for everyone to discover.
Named after Beethoven’s Ode to Joy, the anthem of the European Union, the festival celebrates Europe’s diversity and shared values through the universal language of cinema.
Whether you are a European film enthusiast or simply looking for something different to enjoy in the city, come and experience a little of Europe right here in San Francisco!
Dates: 19–23 November 2026
Venue: Delancey Street Foundation, San Francisco
Admission: Free, with advance registration

events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

THE ART OF TEA CLOSING PARTY
Celebrate the final night of THE ART OF TEA exhibition at HUNT & GATHER Gallery, where a teapot hides in every painting.
Friday, November 20 | 6:00 to 9:00 PM | $95 | 21+ | Limited to 40 guests

Get Tickets

Every painting in Laine Wiesemann’s The Art of Tea hides a teapot. Join us for a closing reception with live jazz, bubbly, blooms, and a tea tower, all in the gallery.

Your ticket includes:

A welcome glass of bubbly (sparkling wine or alcohol-free sparkling tea), with more sparkling wine flowing through the first hour
Live jazz trio
Charcuterie and passed bites
A talk with the artist about her work
A flower bouquet you build yourself at our flower bar
Your own signature tea blend, packaged and labeled to gift or keep
A seated tea tower with a guided tea tasting led by our tea expert

Arrive to bubbly and music, meet Laine, and hunt for her hidden teapots. Make your bouquet and blend your tea. At 7:00, sit down for the tea tower and tasting. Then wander, circle back to anything you missed, and linger over live jazz and a drink from the bar.
The art is for sale

events.title: Honoring Richard: An Organ Benefit Concert
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerCalliope: East Bay Music & ArtsAll proceeds raised during the concert will go toward the Dr. Richard Cushman Organ Scholarship Program.
In honor of Richard’s second heavenly birthday, we’re holding a free benefit concert featuring the students in the scholarship program. Our program, which pays tribute to his legacy, will begin with a pre-concert reception and birthday cake.

The concert will feature a number of his former organ students, as well as current participants in the organ scholarship program founded in his honor, including Arthur Omura, Eileen Chen, Judah Lampkin, and a few special guests!
Dr. Richard Cushman, who died in late December following a tragic accident, was a gifted organist and musician, a beloved teacher, mentor, and friend, as well as a noted scholar of literature.
Presented by Calliope: East Bay Music & Arts

About the Film from the Defiant to the Last website:
“Based on lies and wartime propaganda, during WWII the U.S. government forcibly removed and incarcerated more than 125,000 innocent Japanese Americans in ten American concentration camps, solely because of their race.
“At all the prison sites, despite the mythology of quiet compliance, Japanese Americans showed moral courage, resisted, and refused to accept the government’s abuse. Defiant to the Last tells the story of the Tule Lake Segregation Center where dissident Japanese Americans were demonized and punished for speaking out against the false wartime incarceration.”
Revolution Books is showing this film because the story of resistance to the unjust treatment of the Japanese Americans in WW II resonates deeply with our own time, when immigrants’ rights are stripped away, they are demonized, and some deported to torture prisons in countries they’ve never lived in – and people who oppose this treatment are attacked and vilified by the government.
This is a time for defiance, for voices of conscience to speak out, and for revolution. Defiant to the Last brings crucial experience and important lessons from the past, and we are very glad to be able to bring Satsuki Ina and Emiko Omori to our store.

events.title: Trash Prom Walk of Shame: Runway as Performance Art
events.description:
Jordan Joel

Jordan Joel presents the debut of their newest collection

Trash Prom Walk of Shame
Trash Prom turns shame into spectacle: alchemy, excess and reclamation, built from what the world throws away. The Walk of Shame becomes a walk of pride, a celebration of personal survival in scraps and iridescence.

Here, the discarded is sacred. Trash couture walks alongside upcycled pieces and ready-to-wear, each look in conversation with the others. Together they carry a confession: the things we were told to hide, stitched back together and sent down the runway in full camp glory.
Shame isn’t erased. It’s raw material, and transgression is how it transforms.
Beyond fashion, the night becomes an immersive world of performance art, interactive installations, music and a live atelier.
Join the inaugural Queer Heartstrings, the first iteration of a collective textile creation, and watch transformation happen up close as you become part of the show.
Come as you are, as you were, or as who you’re becoming.
Walk in carrying whatever you’ve been holding, and walk out shining.

The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

events.title: Art of the American West: San Francisco Yarn Art Workshop
events.description:

Join Bay Area–raised, Los Angeles–based contemporary artist Amadour for a free, all-ages art workshop in San Francisco exploring geometric abstraction, Land Art, and the landscapes of the American West. This hands-on family workshop invites visitors of all ages to discover the connections between contemporary art, nature, and creative expression.
Through a lively art history presentation, participants will learn about the work of influential artists of the American West, including Agnes Martin, Nancy Holt, and Michael Heizer, exploring how artists have transformed landscapes through geometry, abstraction, and large-scale interventions in nature.
Following the presentation, participants will experiment with line, shape, color, and space through interactive activities and hands-on yarn art-making, creating their own abstract landscapes to take home.

Amadour is an artist, writer, and musician raised in Reno, Nevada, and Sausalito, California, with Mexican and Colombian roots. Their interdisciplinary practice explores geometric abstraction, architecture, landscape, and the cultural histories of the American West.
Their work has been exhibited internationally, including at KOTARO NUKAGA in Tokyo, The Armory Show in New York, and FF Projects in Mexico. In 2026, they presented Amadour: Nevada Proscenium, a solo exhibition at Truckee Meadows Community College in Reno. events.title: Jack Scott’s 22-Foot Drawings Return After 40 Years (College of Marin)
events.venue: College of Marin Fine Arts Gallery
events.description:
Studio MGHJack Scott: Large-Scale Drawings
Monumental charcoal drawings unseen for forty years return to College of Marin, where the artist began November 16 to December 11, 2026 · Opening reception Saturday, November 21, 3 to 5 pm · College of Marin Fine Arts Gallery, Kentfield, CA
KENTFIELD, CA · Studio MGH and College of Marin present Jack Scott: Large-Scale Drawings, the first public exhibition in forty years of the monumental charcoal drawings Jack Scott made in the 1970s and 1980s. Worked on unstretched unprimed canvas, some reaching 22 feet, each drawing is built from a single repeated mark. Scott developed his own fixative, and four decades later the surfaces remain immaculate. In his time, Scott was one of the most closely watched artists in California. He had solo exhibitions at the Los Angeles Institute of Contemporary Art, Hansen Fuller Goldeen Gallery in San Francisco, and Kirk deGooyer Gallery in Los Angeles. He received a National Endowment for the Arts Artist Fellowship in drawing (1981), was three times a finalist for SFMOMA’s SECA Award (1980, 1981, 1988), and was twice nominated for the Oakland Museum’s Annual Art Award. His work was reviewed in Artforum, the San Francisco Chronicle, the Los Angeles Times, Artweek, and by Rebecca Solnit in the Pacific Sun, and is included in Thomas Albright’s Art in the San Francisco Bay Area, 1945–1980. Robert McDonald wrote in Artweek: “His works must be seen.” Then the drawings, too large and too physical to place easily...

events.title: Book Launch & Talk: Jed Perl & Marius Sosnowski on ‘We Never Called it Frisco’
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerPortrait of Jed Perl. Photo: Duane MichalsTo mark the recent opening of Hauser & Wirth’s new gallery and bookshop in Downtown Palo Alto, please join us for a conversation with Jed Perl and Marius Sosnoski for the launch of Perl’s new book, ‘We Never Called It Frisco,’ from Coffee House Press.
The discussion will explore Perl’s latest novel alongside his acclaimed two-volume biography of Alexander Calder, ‘Calder: The Conquest of Time: The Early Years: 1898-1940,’ and ‘Calder: The Conquest of Space: The Later Years: 1940 – 1976,’ on Calder’s formative years in Los Angeles and San Francisco, and the cultural landscapes that shaped his life and work.

The event takes place alongside ‘Calder | O’Keeffe,’ the inaugural exhibition at Hauser & Wirth’s Palo Alto gallery. Developed in close collaboration with the Calder Foundation, the exhibition brings together exceptional works by Alexander Calder and Georgia O’Keeffe, complemented by archival materials documenting their decades-long friendship.
Copies of ‘We Never Called It Frisco’ and ‘Calder: The Conquest of Time: The Early Years: 1898-1940’ and ‘Calder: The Conquest of Space: The Later Years: 1940 – 1976’ will be available for purchase, and Jed Perl will sign books after the talk.

events.title: Opening Reception: Me, Nature, As One
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerPhoto of artworks courtesy of the artists.Join Qualia Contemporary Art on Saturday, November 21, 2026, for the opening reception of Me, Nature, As One.
Me, Nature, As One is a group exhibition spanning multiple generations whose work traces the evolution and reimagining of shanshui, the classical tradition of landscape painting. Across ink, watercolor, photography, mixed media, and calligraphy, the exhibition presents work that imbues nature with spirituality, internal landscapes, and existential philosophy.

Shanshui, literally “mountain and water,” has never been about depicting nature alone. For centuries, it has sought nature’s spiritual essence and asked a broader question about humanity’s place within it. The featured artists—Victoria Yau, Zhang Yu, Stella Zhang, Meng Huang, Xu Hongming, Jiang Heng, and Chu Chu—reinterpret this classical form while keeping that inquiry alive, guided by the idea that self and nature are not separate but shape one another through subjective experience.

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.address: 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

events.title: Incredible Sugar Castle At The Westin St. Francis
events.description:
The Westin St. FrancisA San Francisco holiday tradition turns 21 this year! Executive Pastry Chef Jean-François Houdré and his team proudly unveil the nearly 12-foot-tall Sugar Castle, a dazzling, handcrafted replica of a French château that has delighted visitors since 2005.
This beloved holiday masterpiece weighs more than 1,000 pounds and features more than 20 towers, approximately 15 illuminated rooms, and a working train, bringing a whimsical French château to life in the heart of Union Square.
New This Year: “Can You Find San Francisco?”
Get ready for a San Francisco treasure hunt! Hidden throughout the Sugar Castle is a replica of the hotel’s beloved dog mascot, Francis, as well as miniature versions of some of the city’s most iconic landmarks, brought to life with custom-designed ornaments generously donated by San Francisco Mercantile. From the Golden Gate Bridge to a classic cable car, guests can find them all, collect the letters, and unscramble the secret word to claim a prize. It’s a playful way for visitors of all ages to discover a little more of San Francisco tucked inside the castle.

Sugar Castle Puzzles
The magic of the Sugar Castle can live on long after the holidays. A one-of-a-kind, custom-made Sugar Castle puzzle captures the intricate details of this beloved San Francisco tradition, inviting visitors to recreate the spectacular confectionery masterpiece piece by piece at home. Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

The Cow Palace, 2600 Geneva Avenue, Daly City, CA

Speakers
Joey Clift is a Los Angeles-based, Peabody and 2x Emmy Award-nominated comedian, writer, director, producer and enrolled member of the Cowlitz Indian Tribe.
Joey attended college to become a local TV weather person because as a kid he didn’t see any Native American comedians on television, and that made him believe he wasn’t allowed to work in comedy. Since then he has learned that this is not true – and his comedy style reflects that. Joey’s work has been featured in The Washington Post, Pitchfork, NPR, Dead Meat, Dropout and Comedy Central.
Terria Smith is a tribal member of the Torres Martinez Desert Cahuilla Indians and a proud original Californian. She is the editor of News from Native California magazine and director of the Berkeley Roundhouse, Heyday’s California Indian publishing program. Smith is also the editor of the 2023 anthology Know We Are Here: Voices of Native California Resistance. She received her undergraduate degree at Cal Poly Humboldt (formerly Humboldt State University) and earned her master’s degree at the UC Berkeley Graduate School of Journalism. She lives on her ancestral homelands in the Coachella Valley with her puppy Havana.

The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

events.title: $1.50 Admission Day for Ripley’s Believe It or Not!’s Final Day in SF
events.venue: Ripley’s Believe It or Not Odditorium
events.description:
Google MapsRipley’s Believe It or Not! is closing its San Francisco Odditorium at Fisherman’s Wharf on Dec. 1, 2026, ending nearly 60 years of strange sights at 175 Jefferson St. The attraction first opened on Feb. 2, 1967, and it’s sending things off with a suitably weird farewell.
On its final day, admission will cost just $1.50 for adults and 75 cents for kids, matching the original 1967 ticket prices. Want to visit before then? Ripley’s is also offering $19.67 admission on Thursdays during its final weeks.
The museum is auctioning off select exhibits and artifacts through a silent auction that stays open until closing. Among the oddities up for grabs are a Golden Gate Bridge made on the head of a pin, toothpick replicas of the bridge, Joe DiMaggio’s crutches, a chicken-wire portrait of Janis Joplin, a matchstick cable car and even a fur-covered fish. There’s also a 1989 Emmy tied to coverage of the Loma Prieta earthquake and World Series.

The building is already being marketed for lease, so the future of this longtime Wharf attraction remains up in the air.
H/t SF Chronicle

events.title: Meet Nina LaCour, Author of Meet Me in the Garden
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerNew Orleans, 1944. Odette has always been one of the Honore sisters, glamorous and admired in their Creole community. But while Odette’s older sisters are content to be wives and mothers, Odette has always wanted something else. It is only with her beloved cousin, Delphine, that Odette can tell her secret: she is in love with a woman, and she longs to be an artist. Delphine has a secret lover, too, a white man. In the hidden garden they’ve discovered, Odette and Delphine can dream of futures full of passion and freedom.
But five years later, Odette’s life is nothing like what she’d planned. She’s a widowed mother, living in Los Angeles, and she and Delphine, who is passing as white, have spiraled away from each other. When Delphine reaches a breaking point, Odette must make a shattering choice to try to hold her family together.

Profound and expansive, a story of love and longing, art and motherhood, friendship and desire, Meet Me in the Garden is a decades-spanning tour de force, inspired by the author’s family and tracing the history of the Great Migration.

The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.title: “Decoder” Film Screening: Analog-Age Anti-Capitalist Riot
events.description:
Submitted by the Event Organizer© Interzone PicturesIn an early cyberpunk version of 1980s Berlin, audiophile F.M. (played by F.M. Einheit of the legendary German noise band Einstürzende Neubauten) spends his nights tuned into the peaceful, unobtrusive Muzak played from nearby H Burger restaurants. But when he discovers that it secretly carries subliminal messages encouraging mindless consumption, he teams up with a group of urban pirates (led by Genesis P-Orridge) to spread a musical antidote. Its patrons awakened from their fast-food slumber and on the edge of all-out anti-capitalist insurrection, H Burger headquarters decides to dispatch a special agent to permanently deal with their F.M. problem.
Inspired by a 1970 essay by William S. Burroughs (who also stars in the film) and featuring the music of Soft Cell, Einstürzende Neubauten, and The The, Decoder doubles as a midnight cult gem and an analog-age riot against the encroachment of technology on the autonomy of human desire and perception.

events.title: Artist Talk with Klea McKenna
events.description: Submitted by the Event OrganizerKlea McKennaJoin us on December 3rd at 6pm for an artist talk with 2025–26 Kala Fellow Klea McKenna. McKenna will share the process of making her installation The Remedy–both how she makes large shaped-plate intaglio prints using cardboard plates–as well as her writing and illustration process. In this work Klea began with the seed of a family story, passed down to her by her maternal line. Using writing and illustration exercises she grew it into a written short story and then a mixed media installation. Klea will share her methods for moving between memory, writing, research and visual imagery. The Remedy is on view in the Kala Gallery as part of What We Hold, New Works by Kala’s 2025-2026 Kala Fellowship artists.
